source.title: On the Spectral Geometry of Cross-Modal Representations: A Functional Map Diagnostic for Multimodal Alignment

record.file_problem: None apparent; the supplied text includes the paper through its references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own cross-modal results and argues that similar spectral complexity does not imply aligned representation bases, refining the convergence claim to partial structural similarity.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures spectral geometry and evaluates mappings between paired image-caption representations. Its retrieval scores are evidence about the evaluated mappings, not a scale sweep. The cited CKA and Platonic Representation Hypothesis results are prior work and are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study measures how DINOv2 and MiniLM/mpnet relate on paired Flickr30k data, and it tests linear mappability with Procrustes, relative representations and functional maps. It argues that convergence is partial: the encoders match in spectral complexity but not in eigenvector orientation. It does not vary model scale or capability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two additions. The authors frame the spectral similarity as consistent with, and complementary to, CKA-based evidence for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They also caveat that it may partly reflect the k-NN graph construction and the finite sample. They call the complexity–orientation gap a structural property of the representations, which bounds purely post-hoc spectral alignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses graph-Laplacian spectra, functional maps, and cross-modal retrieval rather than the original sources' CKA-based or same-architecture representation comparisons; no scale sweep is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval varies with anchor budget and spectral truncation; text-to-image performance does not improve with spectral truncation. Functional-map retrieval is also reported for two text encoders. The graph construction uses one k-NN setting (k=15) and adaptive bandwidth.

fits_no_version.finding: The normalized graph-Laplacian eigenvalue spectra of independently trained vision and text encoders are nearly identical. This is a similarity in intrinsic manifold complexity, not alignment of the representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained encoders of different modalities develop representation manifolds with similar spectral complexity (distribution of variation across scales), even when their bases are unaligned.

record.problems: Only 1,000 images are evaluated; the main anchor-budget results use a single random seed. There is one vision encoder and two text encoders, and only one graph-construction setting. The authors note that larger-scale evaluation and alternative graph constructions may affect the findings.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result bearing on the tested versions was left out. Table 1's additional Recall@5 and Recall@10 values and Table 2's corresponding Recall@5 and Recall@10 values are not separately extracted because they do not change the recorded Recall@1 comparisons. Table 3's eigenvalue ranges are omitted because the normalized spectral distance is the reported summary measure.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and only one vision encoder.
Whether cross-modal alignment rises as both models improve. Only fixed encoder pairs are measured, with no capability variation.
No comparison across seeds or initializations.
No interpretable features or circuits are compared.
Graph construction is fixed at k=15 with adaptive bandwidth. The authors flag possible dependence on graph settings but do not vary them, and they use one dataset.
No test of a plateau or of whether shared data or objectives explain the alignment.
Stitching and unsupervised mappings without paired data are not tested beyond HKS. The only scale is 1,000 samples, with a single seed.

missing.what: Text-to-image R@1 for FMap, Procrustes and relative representations at 20, 100 and 500 anchors (e.g. Procrustes 54.4%, FMap 6.1% at 500).
Full six-budget anchor sweep (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500) for each method, shown only in a figure.
The eigenvalue ratio departs from 1 (up to 1.3) at the lowest frequencies, indices 0–10, and converges toward 1 at higher ones.

record.verdict_notes: The study is a negative result for its own method, so the functional-map rows mainly show that V4 depends on the choice of map. The Procrustes and relative-representation rows are the more direct evidence on V4. There is only one vision encoder, a single seed, 1,000 images and one graph setting.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; only one vision encoder and two text encoders are examined.
Tests cross-modal alignment for a limited set of encoder pairs, but does not vary both models' capability or test whether alignment rises as they improve.
No comparison across random initializations of the same architecture.

Tests spectral functional maps and their composition; does not test stitching, relative representations as a general mapping mechanism, or alignment without paired anchors across the full range of methods named.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.
Does not systematically vary similarity measures, graph settings, or input distributions to test whether a convergence trend changes.
Reports incomplete alignment for independently pretrained encoders, but does not test a scale-dependent plateau or determine whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 + all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rows.stage_stated: independently pretrained; no shared training signal
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized graph-Laplacian eigenvalue spectra
rows.note: The paper interprets the spectra as quantitatively similar, while noting finite-sample and graph-construction caveats.
rows.check: There is no capability trend, so the row cannot bear on V2. It shows only the convergent half: similar normalized Laplacian spectra, 0.043. Read with r2–r3, it gives partial convergence. The authors caution that the similarity may reflect the k-NN graph construction.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 + all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rows.stage_stated: independently pretrained; no shared training signal
rows.operation_detail: Measured diagonal dominance of the functional map
rows.baseline: Near 1 indicates same-index spectral correspondence; shape-matching reference is >0.7
rows.note: The paper describes the eigenvector bases as effectively unaligned; no spectral index reaches 0.2.
rows.check: Drop the V2 link, since there is no capability variation. For V7, the incompleteness is observed: diagonal dominance is below 0.05. The state 'absent' was written against convergence, not against V7.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 + all-MiniLM-L6-v2
rows.stage_stated: independently pretrained; no shared training signal
rows.operation_detail: Measured orthogonality deviation of the functional map
rows.baseline: 0 indicates a perfectly isometric correspondence; near-isometric shape reference is <0.1
rows.note: The paper says the map is not close to orthogonal and the manifolds are not related by a distance-preserving transformation in spectral space.
rows.check: Drop the V2 link. An orthogonality error of 70.15 shows the bases are far from isometric, which is the incompleteness V7 names, so the state for V7 is observed.

relationships.condition: Procrustes and relative representations, DINOv2–MiniLM, Flickr30k, 1,000 images
relationships.reason: Linear mapping depends strongly on the anchor budget. R@1 is 2.1–3.4% at 20 anchors and rises to 55.5% at 500, still below the jointly trained CLIP reference (r7–r12).
relationships.display_finding: R@1 rose from 2.1–3.4% with 20 anchors to 55.5% with 500, remaining below jointly trained CLIP.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Procrustes and relative representations, DINOv2–MiniLM, Flickr30k, 1,000 images
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms strong anchor dependence and incomplete retrieval: 2.1–3.4% R@1 at 20 anchors; 55.5% for Procrustes and 26.6% for relative representations at 500. CLIP is a supervised reference, not a controlled estimate of mapping loss.

relationships.condition: Functional maps (linear maps between Laplacian spectral bases), DINOv2 with MiniLM or mpnet
relationships.reason: Image-to-text R@1 stays at 0.5–4.3%, and text-to-image R@1 without ZoomOut is at chance for ks≥20. Composing maps through a third encoder degrades retrieval further. So mappability depends on the choice of map (r4–r6, r14, r16–r31).
relationships.display_finding: Spectral maps yielded image-to-text R@1 of 0.5–4.3% and chance-level text-to-image retrieval without ZoomOut at spectral dimensions of at least 20; composition through a third encoder degraded retrieval further.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Functional maps (linear maps between Laplacian spectral bases), DINOv2 with MiniLM or mpnet
source_check.reason: Split this mixed condition group: retain limits_scope for above-baseline but weak retrieval (r4–r6, r14, r16–r22, r28–r30; Tables 1–5), and assign challenges specifically to text-to-image retrieval without ZoomOut at ks≥20, where R@1 is 0.0–0.1%, at or below the 0.1% baseline (r23–r27). The failure applies to the tested spectral maps.

relationships.condition: DINOv2–MiniLM on Flickr30k, ks=50, k=15 graph
relationships.reason: Spectra are similar (0.043), but diagonal dominance is below 0.05 and orthogonality error is 70.15. Convergence is incomplete: complexity is shared, orientation is not (r1–r3).
relationships.display_finding: Spectral discrepancy was 0.043, but diagonal dominance stayed below 0.05 and orthogonality error reached 70.15.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: DINOv2–MiniLM on Flickr30k, ks=50, k=15 graph
source_check.reason: Table 3 confirms spectral distance 0.043, mean diagonal dominance below 0.05 and orthogonality error 70.15, supporting incomplete convergence. Plateauing and shared-training causes are untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
